Hannah (Finance): Received invoice from BrightWave NL (BW-9302). Shows 0% VAT, Dutch VAT ID, but vendor is asking us to gross-up for 'US tax withholding'. Any guidance?

invoice-bot: New invoice #BW-9302 1799998759 EUR 24,500 vendor VAT: NL123456789B01

Marta (Vendor Ops): Invoice notes say 'reverse charge applies'. That fits B2B EU if billed to our NL entity. Gross-up ask seems unrelated to VAT.

Liam (Tax): Yepgross-up = withholding issue, not VAT. If payment from Redwood Inc (US), vendor might expect withholding; they'd need W-8BEN-E. If billed to Redwood B.V. and paid from EU, reverse charge applies and no VAT due. Ask for proof of VAT registration and clarify billed entity.

Sam (Accounting): Invoice header: Invoice BW-9302, 2026-02-28, Billed to Redwood B.V. (NL987654321B02), Amount EUR24,500, VAT 0% reverse charge.

Hannah (Finance): Draft reply: "We cannot gross-up by default. Please confirm billed entity (Redwood B.V. vs Redwood Inc), provide VAT registration certificate and tax residency docs. If payment is from a US entity and you expect no withholding, submit W-8BEN-E. If contract requires gross-up, include clause." Thoughts?

Marta (Vendor Ops): Sending request now and placing payment on hold pending docs.

invoice-bot: Payment hold: reason vendor tax docs missing

Liam (Tax): If vendor insists on gross-up, escalate to Legal.

Hannah (Finance): Agree. Will close when vendor returns docs. :thumbsup:
